messages:
sam: FYI -- the TypeScript sample-app fails on Edge deployments after we merged the new package exports change in the JS SDK.
sam: Build error in Vercel Edge function: `Error: Cannot find module '@redwood/inference-js'` at runtime, and tsc also complains about missing types.

tara: Can you paste the minimal repro + package.json from the SDK in the node_modules tree? Is this only happening on Edge or also in node dev?

sam: Only on Edge (local node dev works). Repro steps: new sample-app (next13 edge runtime) -> `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'` -> deploy.
Error and package snippet I saw in dist package.json:

```
"name": "@redwood/inference-js",
"version": "2.0.0",
"main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
"module": "dist/index.esm.js",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.esm.js",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
  }
}
```

sam: Edge bundler seems to prefer the "import" condition and then the framework's bundler (SWC/ESBuild) inlines it weirdly, but the deployed runtime then throws because the published package didn't include the ESM entry in a format the Edge packager expects (maybe missing .mjs extension?).

zack: I ran into something similar. Some edge runtimes (and older vercel builders) expect the entrypoint to be .mjs for pure ESM, and others prefer an import map that includes a "default" or a browser conditional. Two quick fixes:
- publish ESM as .mjs alongside .js
- or add an exports conditional for "browser" and "edge" that points to a bundled ESM file that the Edge toolchain can consume.

zack: Example export tweak that helped another lib:

```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs.js",
    "browser": "dist/index.browser.mjs"
  }
}
```

monica: TS side: tsc complains "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference-js'" even though types field exists. In our case the ESM entry was resolved first but the published package didn't actually include dist/index.d.ts in the ESM bundle path. We need to ensure types are shipped and that `types` points to a file present for both conditions. Otherwise consumers using `moduleResolution: node16` will fail.

sam: So is the plan to revert the exports change or to patch the package to include explicit edge/browser entries + .mjs ESM files? Which is lower risk for us?

zack: Patch + publish a 2.0.1 that adds dedicated edge/browser condition and ships dist/*.mjs and dist/*.d.ts. Should be backward-compatible since require still points to cjs.

monica: I'll open a PR to the SDK repo with these changes and add a small smoke test: a Next/Edge integration that does a static import and runs in the vercel builder (we can run it in CI using the vercel cli builder emulation).

sam: Great. For the sample-app temporary workaround can we change imports to `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs.js'`? Ugly but quick.

zack: That will work for now. Also note we should add a note in the changelog: "If you target Edge runtimes, upgrade to 2.0.1 which includes `browser`/`edge` exports and .mjs ESM entrypoints." 

devx-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/842 (automated)

monica: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1256 - adds .mjs, explicit exports, and a small edge smoke test. @zack can you review? :eyes:

zack: Reviewing now.

sam: Thanks everyone — I'll patch the sample-app readme with the workaround and add a short note in onboarding docs so new users don't hit this.

tara: Filed a doc task to add an "Edge compatibility" section to SDK onboarding checklist.

sam: Resolving for now, will follow up if the vercel builder still trips. :thumbsup:
